text: EvidenceOps uses FastEmbed for local dense embeddings with CPU-optimized execution. The embedding model generates vector representations for indexed document chunks without external network calls. Chunk embeddings are persisted directly into local vector storage.

The sparse index in EvidenceOps is implemented using rank-bm25 for lexical matching. BM25 scores keyword frequency against document frequency across corpus segments. The index is stored locally as serialized structures.

Qdrant runs as a local vector database instance communicating over HTTP or gRPC. It manages collection schemas, payload filtering, and cosine similarity distance metrics. Vector payloads preserve chunk identifiers and provenance metadata.

LangGraph orchestrates bounded multi-step retrieval workflows without unbounded agent loops. Each graph node represents a deterministic transformation or retrieval step. The state graph enforces a hard limit of three retrieval calls per request. Graph execution halts immediately when budget limits are encountered.

FlashRank performs local cross-encoder reranking over candidate chunks. The reranker orders combined dense and sparse candidates by semantic relevance score. Reranking operates entirely on CPU without requiring GPU acceleration. The top ranked candidates form the final retrieval context.

FastAPI powers the EvidenceOps HTTP backend with typed request schemas. Endpoints validate input queries, source parameters, and budget constraints. Responses emit structured JSON payloads adhering to OpenAPI contracts. Middleware enforces loopback locality boundaries for administrative endpoints.

OpenTelemetry instruments all retrieval pipelines with structured spans. Traces capture span durations, query parameters, and cache hit metrics. The Jaeger exporter sends trace spans to local Jaeger instances for visualization. Sensitive queries and credentials are automatically redacted before span emission.

Document ingestion splits source markdown files into fixed-size chunks with configurable overlap. Chunks preserve heading breadcrumbs and document lineage identifiers. Markdown tables and code blocks are extracted with structural boundaries preserved. Ingested files are recorded in dataset manifests with SHA-256 hashes.

LiteBridge Core defines the ContextPackage schema and the prepare_context facade. Context preparation executes retrieval and returns immutable evidence packages. The facade operates in a generator-independent manner without invoking language models. All citation markers and source URIs are preserved in the returned package.

Deterministic planning selects retrieval routes based on query cues and budget availability. Local reference cues direct queries toward local documentation sources. Freshness cues direct queries toward web retrieval when consent is granted. Budget preflight rejects requests when call or cost limits are exhausted.

Extractive context compression prunes redundant sentences while retaining original evidence identifiers. Exact duplicate evidence records are filtered when deduplication is enabled. Non-consecutive citation identifiers remain valid after compression. Target context size is enforced against the final rendered output.

The local configuration file config.json defines active profiles and retrieval limits. Default profiles enforce local-only execution with zero external network connectivity. Hybrid execution profiles allow registered web search when explicit consent is provided. Cache configurations specify TTL and maximum entry bounds.

Source descriptors in LiteBridge register metadata including freshness, privacy, and cost. Each registered source has a unique identifier and supported execution profiles. The source registry validates that connectors implement the EvidenceRetriever interface. Connector failures emit standardized diagnostic events.

The EvidenceOps Python SDK provides typed client bindings for local and hybrid pipelines. Clients interact with the LiteBridge facade using structured request models. Internal adapter classes and database connections are hidden behind facade boundaries. Connection exceptions are caught and converted to domain errors.

Local documentation indexing indexes markdown files located in the docs/ directory. Relative file links are normalized to standard documentation paths. Indexing generates term frequency matrices and vector embeddings concurrently. The indexing pipeline reports elapsed time and chunk counts upon completion.

Model evaluation benchmarks measure retrieval accuracy, recall, and context density. Evaluation runners compare pipeline outputs against frozen ground truth datasets. Metric calculations include route selection accuracy and evidence ID recall. Benchmark reports output JSON summaries with environment metadata.

Budget tracking decrements available call and cost allowances per retrieval operation. When retrieval calls reach zero, further operations are halted with BUDGET_EXCEEDED. Web search operations deduct configured micro-USD costs from external budgets. Cache hits do not increment call counts or deduct external cost.

The FastMCP server exposes narrow evidence retrieval tools to MCP client applications. Tool arguments are strictly validated with extra fields forbidden. Server initialization binds to loopback interfaces to prevent remote exploitation. Context packages are accessed through opaque server-issued context handles.

Security policy prohibits transmission of private evidence to external services without explicit consent. Local document excerpts remain on-premise under local-only execution profiles. Hosted LLM adapters require per-call authorization before evidence export. Log messages sanitize authentication headers and API tokens.

Cache key generation computes deterministic SHA-256 hashes over normalized query text and filters. In-memory cache entries expire according to configured time-to-live seconds. Cache eviction removes oldest entries when maximum storage capacity is reached. Cache hits bypass retrieval adapters and return existing packages.

Error handling defines specific domain exceptions for retrieval failures and budget exhaustion. Exceptions carry descriptive messages without leaking internal system paths. Unhandled errors are caught at service boundaries and transformed into structured responses. Diagnostics log error types with correlated trace identifiers.

Extractive sentence pruning identifies high-scoring sentences using lexical overlap with query tokens. Lower scoring sentences are removed until the target character limit is satisfied. Retained sentences maintain their original relative order within each evidence item. Punctuation and sentence boundaries are preserved accurately.

Interface package store provides thread-safe in-memory caching of prepared context packages. Each stored package receives an unguessable opaque context handle prefixed with ctx_. Handles expire automatically after configured time-to-live intervals. Package retrieval using deterministic package IDs is deliberately rejected.
